  "hypothesis": "Predicted that participants reminded of God (high God salience condition) would show a lower preference for human recommendations versus algorithmic recommendations compared to participants in the low God salience condition.",
  "design": "between-subjects with two conditions: high God salience and low God salience",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Writing task about the role or impact of God in their lives (high salience) versus writing about things done during the day (low salience)",
  "outcome_measure": "Relative preference for relying on a human recommendation versus an algorithm's recommendation across 24 different tasks, indicated on a 101-point scale",
  "population_and_setting": "US-based participants recruited on Prolific",
  "sample_size_total": 321,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Recruited online via Prolific in return for monetary payment",
  "analysis_plan": "A one-way ANOVA on an index score computed by averaging responses across the 24 decisions, and a multiple linear regression analysis regressing recommendation preferences on God salience while controlling for task characteristics",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "preregistered",
  "other_methods_notes": "Participants also rated tasks on objectivity, consequentialness, and uniqueness, and completed a God salience manipulation check and demographic measures."
